page: Microsoft Azure M8-2ms is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8280L processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 219.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 109.38 GB per physical core. A 275 GB local SSD is included for temporary local storage, while GPU acceleration is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark results highlight an asymmetric performance profile governed by the modest compute capacity. Multi-core compute benchmarks reflect the two-thread constraint, with Geekbench multi-core registering 1059.0 and stress-ng multi-core achieving 1351.6. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 75.49 GB/sec for small cached blocks, decreasing to 9.62 GB/sec for large uncached read transfers and 8.08 GB/sec for uncached write operations. Key-value operations measured via Redis SET throughput reach 1.27 million operations per second.

The hardware configuration represents an extreme capacity-over-compute tradeoff. Because processing resources are limited to 2 vCPUs, deploying compute-intensive tasks, parallel compilers, or active machine learning jobs on this instance is inefficient relative to its memory tier. Instead, the M8-2ms is primarily designed for workloads that demand substantial memory capacity with low processing concurrency, such as large memory-resident caching layers, state stores, and read-heavy in-memory datasets.
description: Microsoft Azure M8-2ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon 8280L processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The system provides an exceptionally high memory-to-core allocation, offering 219.0 GB of total RAM alongside 275 GB of local SSD storage. No dedicated GPUs are included. Performance testing demonstrates that compute capacity is heavily restricted by the two-thread limit, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 1059.0 and stress-ng multi-core reaching 1351.6. Memory bandwidth achieves 75.49 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 9.62 GB/sec for large uncached read transfers, while Redis SET operations handle 1.27 million operations per second. With its vast memory allocation paired with minimal processor power, the M8-2ms presents a clear tradeoff favoring memory footprint over computational processing, making it suited for large-footprint in-memory caches, quiet memory-resident datasets, and workloads with modest compute demands.
